filed_hypothesis: ADVISORY. The cheap half is exposure, not implementation: most of these commands already work and only lack a path from the `kuna` binary. The expensive half is the stubs.
decisions: THE ACCEPTANCE PROBE THIS NEED HAS NEVER HAD IS FILED: a-567d3207ce62, and it is the deliverable the captain called load-bearing. acceptance_id was null, so no B_DONE could have closed the need whatever shipped. It asserts two range facts on one `kuna decompile --json` and both are diffs of the emitted C, not return codes. FAILS at ed353fb2 (exit 2, `unknown directive "readonly"`), PASSES here, promoted verbatim to tests/cli/no-cli-data-code-override.json.

SECTION 6 OF THE --assert PROPOSAL WAS WRONG ABOUT WHY, AND THE REASON IS THE MOST IMPORTANT FINDING HERE. It reported readonly/volatile as 'accepted; no fold on the fixture tried' and concluded no in-repo fixture shows an observable effect. The effect is real; the ORDER was wrong. `Scope::addMap` folds the range property into each SymbolEntry as it maps it (kuna database.rs:1979, C++ database.cc:1156-1158) and never consults the range again, and the per-function global snapshot then reads the SYMBOL's flags. So a `readonly` painted AFTER `read symbols` is silently inert over every address the loader named -- which is every address a caller is likely to name. Painted BEFORE, the same command on the same fixture folds. Measured both ways on a purpose-built fixture and on a stripped copy of it (stripped: works either way, because there is no symbol to shadow the range).

THAT FORCED A FOURTH SCRIPT SLOT. Stage A's slots are Program (after `read symbols`), Function (after `load function`) and Symbol (after the first `decompile`). A range property fits none of them; `Slot::Image` emits it after `load file`+`option` and before `read symbols`. The in-process surface cannot use that ordering at all -- `bootstrap_from_object` reads the loader's symbols before a caller can say anything -- so `assertions::paint_property` re-applies the property to the symbols the range covers (find_overlap + set_attribute, whose mask already admits readonly/volatil). Both surfaces were then measured emitting byte-identical C.

A `readonly` DIRECTIVE TURNS READ-ONLY PROPAGATION ON FOR THE RUN. Painting the property is only half of it: `Funcdata::fillin_read_only` is gated on the program-wide `readonly` option, which is default-off, so `--assert 'readonly ...'` alone would have been accepted-and-inert -- the exact failure this plane exists to end. It is applied ahead of the caller's own `--option`s (an `option readonly on` line before them on the script surface; `arch.readonlypropagate = true` before apply_runtime_options in-process), so an explicit `--option readonly off` still wins. Both directions are tested. The reverse composition is NOT equivalent and that is the point of the control test: `--option readonly on` with no range folds nothing here, because the loader marks read-only from section flags and .data is writable.

THE `global` DIRECTIVE IS DELIBERATELY NOT SHIPPED, and this is a measurement, not a scope cut. `global add`/`global remove` ARE wired here (the stubs named ScopeGlobal range add/remove; Database::add_range/remove_range have been ported and public in p0_knowledge/database.rs all along -- ~15 lines each, the second half of the Hypothesis overturned again). But wiring them shows `global add` is measurably a NO-OP on any ordinary image: every stock cspec's <global> claims the whole default data space (x86-64-gcc.cspec `<range space="ram"/>`, ARM.cspec the same), so the range is global before the caller speaks. Only `global remove` moves the C -- it kills a store that survives a call. A directive that is accepted and does nothing is the thing this family is being fixed for, so `global` stays off the plane and the two commands stay console-only, with an end-to-end test asserting the C changed in both directions.

THE SYMPTOM'S OWN FRAMING OF `global add` IS WRONG and is recorded as such on the need: it adds a range to the global DATA scope, not to code. 'Marking a gap as code' is `--define-function` / `function bounds`, shipped by #374. The round-1 need this one cites as its motivation (runtime-decrypted-code-opaque) wants the boundary lever, not this one.

THE CONSOLE COMMANDS TAKE AN EXPLICIT SIZE AFTER THE ADDRESS, a small additive divergence from C++ IfcReadonly/IfcVolatile, because the alternative was worse. C++ takes the size only from the bracketed `[space,offset,size]` form, which forces the caller to name the address space -- and `build_script` runs before the image is loaded, so the CLI does not know it. `readonly 0x404028 8` (leading 0 selects the default code space) is what a directive lowers to. Strictly additive: a trailing token was previously ignored, and the two corpus uses are both bracketed.

THE `data` DIRECTIVE THE PROPOSAL PARKED IN STAGE B ALREADY SHIPPED IN STAGE A, so Stage B is readonly + volatile, not four directives. `type varnode` (the need's fifth named command) is reachable as Stage A's `type` for a local; its usepoint/[space,offset,size] form is recorded as residue rather than given a second spelling nobody asked for.

NO OPTION, NO STAGES TESTCASE, NO CATALOG COUNTERS, NO DIV ROW. A CLI surface cannot change emitted C on its own, which is the tooling track's rule and what Stage A shipped under; phases.toml / docs/options.md / the DIV registry / the catalog counts were all leased by the sibling quality builder this wave in any case. phases.toml's P1 code-data-partition exposure prose now names two commands that work rather than two stubs, but the prose itself is left to whoever holds the lease.

REJECTED -- range-scoped folding via `Architecture::dynreloc_const`. That field is documented as 'offsets whose read-only contents fold even with readonlypropagate off' (the PT_GNU_RELRO exception), is set from kuna-console (engine.rs:2100), and appending the asserted ranges to it would have given exactly range-scoped folding with no program-wide change. Not taken: the field is named for dynrelocs and reusing it without renaming would leave a reader finding --assert ranges in a list that says otherwise, while renaming it means editing three kuna-decomp files the sibling quality builder has declared this wave. The option route is the shipped, documented, agent-reachable one and the broadening is sound (a range the loader marks read-only from section flags really is read-only), so it is the honest choice here; if the breadth ever bites, the precise mechanism is one rename away.
mechanism: Two directives on the Stage-A `--assert` plane -- `readonly <addr>+<size>` and `volatile <addr>+<size>` -- plus a fourth script slot for them and the wiring of the `global add`/`global remove` stubs. kuna-console/src/assertions.rs gains Body::Readonly/Body::Volatile at P1 code-data-partition and `paint_property`, which ORs the Varnode property over [addr, addr+size) via Database::set_property_range and then re-applies it to every global symbol the range covers (find_overlap + set_attribute), because Scope::addMap absorbed the old value at map time. kuna-cli/src/assertdecl.rs parses `<addr>+<size>` (and `<addr> <size>`, decimal or hex) and lowers each to `Slot::Image`, emitted between the `option` lines and `read symbols`. A `readonly` directive also turns read-only propagation on ahead of the caller's own options (kuna_console::assertions::implies_readonly_propagation, consulted by both surfaces), since fillin_read_only is gated on it. kuna-console/src/ifacedecomp.rs: `readonly`/`volatile` accept an explicit size after the address, and IfcGlobalAdd/IfcGlobalRemove call Database::add_range/remove_range on the global scope instead of returning engine_unavailable.

measurements.method: drove decompiler/target/release/decomp_dbg and the built `kuna` binary directly, one command per line on stdin, on a purpose-built in-repo fixture; every verdict is a diff of the printed C, never a return code. Both CLI surfaces measured separately: `kuna decompile` forks decomp_dbg through the generated script, `kuna decompile --json` loads in-process.
measurements.fixture: decompiler/crates/kuna-analysis/tests/fixtures/assertranges_x86_64 (15800 bytes, source vendored beside it): `sample` reads two .data globals nothing writes and reads 0x50000000 twice; `latch` stores 0x50000004, calls, reads it back
measurements.baseline_sample: int sample(int a0) { return scale * a0 + bias + dat_50000000 * 2; }
measurements.volatile_only: v1 = dat_50000000; return scale * a0 + bias + v1 + dat_50000000;
measurements.both: v1 = dat_50000000; return a0 * 7 + 100 + v1 + dat_50000000;  (identical on both surfaces)
measurements.control_option_alone: `--option readonly on` with no range: baseline, unchanged -- the range is what does the work
measurements.control_explicit_off: `--assert 'readonly 0x404028+8' --option readonly off`: baseline, unchanged -- an explicit option wins
measurements.global_remove: latch: `dat_50000004 = a0; ext(); return dat_50000004;` -> `ext(); return a0;`
measurements.global_add_after_remove: restores the store; `global add` with no prior remove changes nothing on any stock cspec

speed: zero on every existing invocation: no directive means no extra console line, no property paint and an empty assertions[]. A range directive adds one console line and one symbol-table walk over the range (one lookup per covered symbol, not per byte) before any decompile; no pipeline pass is added and no extra decompile is emitted -- these are image-scoped, so unlike the symbol-scoped directives they never force the second pass.
risks: a readonly directive turns read-only propagation on for the whole run, so the loader's own read-only ranges (.rodata, RELRO) fold too. That is what `--option readonly on` has always meant and it is only reached by passing a directive; an explicit `--option readonly off` still wins. Folding a genuinely read-only range is sound -- the option is default-off for upstream parity, not for correctness.

the property is a caller ASSERTION and kuna cannot check it: marking a range read-only that the program does write produces wrong C. The engine already warns on the written case (`Read-only address (...) is written`) rather than folding it.

the explicit-size extension to the console `readonly`/`volatile` commands diverges from C++ IfcReadonly. Additive -- a trailing token was previously ignored -- and the datatest corpus's only two uses are bracketed, which the parity gate confirms.
blast radius is nil: nothing here runs unless a directive is passed or the console command is typed, and the parity corpora are symbol-less bytechunks driven by XML with no CLI in the loop.
